corrections.how: Run Home Assistant OS in a VM on the Mac mini (the roadmap already plans this VM for the kids' speaker). Add the Hue, Sonos and LG webOS integrations, then the 'Model Context Protocol Server' integration; turn off 'Expose all LLM APIs' and expose only the wanted entities. In OpenClaw add mcp.servers.<name> with url http://<ha-host>:8123/api/mcp, transport 'streamable-http' written out (when it is omitted OpenClaw uses sse), and the Home Assistant long-lived token in headers.Authorization, supplied through a secret reference and not a config literal (auth 'oauth' with openclaw mcp login is the documented alternative). This Gateway uses tools.profile 'minimal', which hides MCP tools, so grant them only to the stateless 'home' agent from F076 by listing the <server>__<tool> names in that agent's alsoAllow and in its sandbox tool allow list (tools.sandbox.tools.alsoAllow); no other agent then sees the server. Write toolFilter.include after a live probe (openclaw mcp doctor <name> --probe), since it selects tools by name. The registry before_tool_call hook stays as the second, fail-closed gate and enforces quiet hours.
caveats: Home Assistant's MCP options 'Expose all LLM APIs' and 'Require an administrator account' are both on by default: out of the box every LLM API is offered and the token must belong to an administrator. Tighten the first before OpenClaw connects; a token for a non-admin Home Assistant user works only after the second is turned off.
The MCP server does not support notifications or sampling, so Home Assistant cannot push a state change to Happy through MCP; events need a separate webhook (see HOM-06).
A HomeKit accessory can pair with only one controller, so the LG TV stays in Apple Home and joins Home Assistant through the webOS integration, not through HomeKit.

Home Assistant's macOS page is written for people who already run a supported hypervisor (VirtualBox, with UTM as the fallback) and points everyone else to a dedicated board; the VM is one more service to patch and back up.
Running both the direct CLIs and Home Assistant doubles the paths to the same lamp; pick one.
With only Hue, two Sonos and one TV today, the hub pays off mainly if presence (HOM-05), announcements (HOM-03) or the kids' speaker are also wanted.

toolFilter selects MCP tools by name, not by device. Home Assistant's LLM API works through intents, so one tool may act on any exposed entity; the per-device limit lives in Home Assistant's exposure list and in the hook, not in toolFilter.

corrections.description: A guardrail to set before any family iPhone, personal or the spare one, is paired with the Gateway. The iOS platform default lets a paired iPhone answer location, contact search, calendar events, reminders, latest photos and motion queries with no Gateway allow entry, once the node's command surface is approved and the matching switch and iOS permission are on in the app; only camera capture, screen recording, writes and Health need an explicit allow.
corrections.how: List everything a phone should not answer in gateway.nodes.commands.deny (deny always wins), and add to gateway.nodes.commands.allow only the single command a feature needs. Both lists are Gateway-wide: an allow entry applies to every paired node that declares the command, so per-phone narrowing relies on the switches in each phone's app (the iPhone camera switch is on by default) and on which command surface is approved. Pair personal phones with openclaw qr --limited, which drops only operator.admin and leaves the phone a chat and approvals client; for a spare or room device try --voice-node, which hands off only operator.read and operator.talk. Review and approve each node's command surface explicitly (openclaw nodes pending, openclaw nodes approve). Grant the nodes tool only to the agent that needs it, and have the registry before_tool_call hook block any call whose node is not the one assigned to that agent.
caveats: The default table is a ceiling, not a promise: a command works only if the phone app also declares it, but a later app update can start declaring more.
A phone paired with the default (full) setup code also becomes an admin client of the Gateway.
An operator client with write scope can invoke enabled node commands directly, not only agents.
The App Store build registers with OpenClaw's hosted push relay for background wakes, so a paired iPhone adds one outside service that the Gateway talks to.
unverified: No documented per-agent setting was found that limits which node the nodes tool may target, so the hook pin is assumed to be necessary.

corrections.how: Create one persistent 'board' session on an agent with no tools beyond reading the home-store. An agent-turn automation targeted at that session (--session session:<id>) with an explicit tool cap (--tools show_widget plus the store read tool) replaces named native report widgets (metrics, table, text and link blocks) with pin set to true. Save the expanded dashboard as the session's shared default (Layout, 'Use current view as default', or the dashboard tool's set_default_presentation action) so every open shows the board without a special link. The display is a browser on a spare tablet, signed in to the tailnet, that opens the Control UI through Tailscale Serve at that session; its device token is rotated down to a read scope (operator.read, or the narrower operator.sessions.read if that proves enough), and the tablet is locked to the browser with Guided Access. For lights and speaker state, a Home Assistant dashboard is the simpler second page.
caveats: show_widget is offered only to clients that declare inline widgets, or to a scheduled job bound to a persistent session and limited to pinned widgets; a parent cannot text Happy over iMessage and get a widget.
A Control UI on the wall is an operator client of the whole Gateway; unless its scope is read-only, anyone in the kitchen can chat with an agent from it.
A native report is capped at 24 blocks and 8 KB, with no scripts or images.
The ?dashboard=expanded link applies to that visit only; the saved shared default is the durable way to open the board expanded. A page reload starts fresh widget views.
The macOS panel needs the OpenClaw Mac app (not installed), shows one panel at a time near the menu bar and is render-only.
The Website widget needs an HTTPS address and refuses the Gateway's own host, so a plain-HTTP Home Assistant page cannot be embedded.
Guests see whatever is on it: first names and times only, no addresses, no health or money lines.
A printed week sheet (F080, HOM-14) gives most of the benefit with no screen to keep alive.

corrections.how: Route A: an allowlisted Shortcut named 'TV off' in happy's account, run with the shortcuts command by the F078 plugin; happy's Apple Account must be a member of the Home, and a member without remote control can act only while at home on the home network, which is where the Mac mini sits. Route A can switch the TV off but cannot show a message. Route B (needs HOM-01): Home Assistant's webOS media player turns the TV off or changes volume, and the on-screen line is the per-TV notify action. Because the MCP server works through Assist intents, put 'show notice N, wait, turn off' into one Home Assistant script whose only field picks from fixed strings, and expose that script. Power-on is left out. Scheduled runs are command or home-agent jobs with a skip-tonight file, as in F081.
caveats: The TV is the only HomeKit accessory in the house, so this is the whole of 'HomeKit control' today.
Apple Home can switch an accessory off at a time of day only when a home hub (HomePod or Apple TV) is set up, and none is in the inventory.
The webOS integration cannot power the TV on by itself (it needs Wake-on-LAN) and requires the TV's 'LG Connect Apps' setting.
Because a HomeKit accessory pairs with one controller, the Home Assistant route uses LG's own network API, not HomeKit.
The remote on the sofa is still the fastest off switch; the value is the scheduled, argument-free cut-off.
The on-screen notice is available only through Home Assistant (Route B); the HomeKit Shortcut route can only switch the TV off or change what HomeKit exposes.

Fetched the abstract. Indirect prompt injection through emails, calendar invitations and shared documents against Gemini-powered assistants, with control of home automation devices among the outcomes; the vendor's mitigations are said to reduce risk to very low to medium.
Read lines 17-67. A before_tool_call handler receives the call parameters and can return block, which is terminal.

corrections.how: Three independent blocks that a model cannot talk its way past. In Home Assistant: turn off exposing new entities to Assist, review the exposure list after every device is added (the cover domain, which holds garage doors and gates, is exposed by default; locks, alarm panels and cameras are not), and turn off the MCP option that exposes every LLM API. On the OpenClaw side: toolFilter.include keeps the imported MCP tools to a short named list and the Shortcut name allowlist (F078) leaves out anything touching those devices. And the registry before_tool_call hook inspects each call's parameters and returns block for any entity, area or device type on the never list, failing closed. toolFilter works on tool names only, so on its own it cannot keep a general 'turn on' or 'open' tool away from a garage door.
unverified: The default exposure set was read from the development branch of Home Assistant's source; confirm it on the installed release before relying on it.

corrections.how: Install the OpenClaw iOS app on the spare iPhone under happy's Apple Account and pair it with the narrowest setup code that works: openclaw qr --voice-node (node credentials plus read and talk scopes only) if the app accepts it, otherwise --limited, which still leaves a chat-capable client on the windowsill. Add camera.snap to gateway.nodes.commands.allow and deny every other phone command (HOM-08); the allow entry applies to every paired node, so switch the camera off in the app on any personal iPhone that is also paired. Keep the app in the foreground with Guided Access (touch disabled) and the app's keep-awake setting. The adult's main agent requests a snapshot through the nodes tool with the back camera selected, because the default is the front camera; the JPEG (1600 px wide by default) goes to the vision model and the answer is one line with the picture. No motion watching.
caveats: Camera commands work only while the app is in the foreground; a backgrounded app returns NODE_BACKGROUND_UNAVAILABLE.
Through glass at night the picture is mostly reflection.
A phone kept awake on a charger all year is a maintenance item of its own.
Outward-facing only; an always-available camera inside rooms where the kids are is not appropriate.
A low-cost network camera with camsnap (F079) is sturdier and can watch for motion; camsnap can also read a local webcam on the Mac.

The app on the spare phone is also a Gateway client: with a limited code anyone at the phone can chat with an agent, and even the voice-node profile allows starting a voice session, so Guided Access with touch disabled is what keeps the kids out.
